overall: Tomorrow (July 5) is expected to be another dangerously hot day in Washington, DC, with the Heat Advisory extending through 8:00PM EDT. The NWS forecasts a high near 97°F with heat index values up to 104°F, and a 40% chance of afternoon thunderstorms developing after 3pm, which could briefly suppress the peak temperature. Overnight lows tonight will only fall to around 77°F, leaving a warm base heading into Sunday.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model divergence: European-leaning models (ECMWF ~88.3°F, GEM ~89.7°F, WEATHER_COM ~89.2°F) are considerably cooler than the American operational suite (GFS ~95.6°F, HRRR ~94.0°F, NBM ~95.0°F), producing a wide ensemble spread and a blended expected TMAX of only 91.1°F — well below the NWS text forecast of 97°F. The persistent Heat Advisory and today's observed TMAX of 100.4°F favor the warmer American model cluster over the cooler European guidance.
max_temp_prediction: The active Kalshi market uses odd buckets, with the top odd bucket at 97-98°F (18.9% probability), but both even and odd bucket sets are classified as Tier 4 (Poor Signals — AVOID) due to high entropy and low top-bucket probability, indicating a very uncertain and spread-out distribution. Weighing the NWS narrative (near 97°F), the GFS/HRRR/NBM cluster (~94-96°F), the extended Heat Advisory, and the warm overnight low, the most likely high is in the 95-97°F range; afternoon storm activity introduces meaningful downside risk toward the low-to-mid 90s if convection arrives earlier than forecast. Confidence is low given significant inter-model disagreement and the Tier 4 signal quality.
